items.summary: libgphoto2 through 2.5.34 contains a stack buffer overflow in sierra_get_string_register() that lets a malicious sierra-protocol camera or USB device overwrite stack memory. When files are listed, the device can answer the file-name register with an oversized packet, writing up to 32 KB past small stack buffers to cause crashes or possible code execution.
items.title: libgphoto2 through 2.5.34 Stack Buffer Overflow via sierra_get_string_register()

items.summary: edbrowse through 3.8.19 contains an integer overflow in stringAndBytes() that allows malicious servers to write past a heap buffer by sending response bodies larger than 2 GB. When a user browses to an attacker-controlled HTTP, FTP, or gopher server, the oversized body skips reallocation and corrupts the heap, causing crashes or potentially code execution.
items.title: edbrowse through 3.8.19 Heap Buffer Overflow via stringAndBytes() Integer Overflow

items.summary: Gammu before 1.45.2 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in ReadBackupTextLen() that allows attackers to overwrite stack memory via crafted backup files. Attackers can supply overlong quoted text values decoded into a 10,000-byte stack array during convertbackup, restore, or GSM_ReadBackupFile calls, causing crashes or potential code execution.
items.title: Gammu before 1.45.2 Stack-Based Buffer Overflow via ReadBackupTextLen()

items.summary: Gammu before 1.45.2 contains a buffer overflow vulnerability in LoadBackup() that allows attackers to corrupt memory by supplying an overlong MD5 value in a crafted backup file. Attackers can overwrite adjacent phonebook and calendar entry pointers via strcpy() into MD5Original when files are loaded with convertbackup or restore, causing crashes or potential code execution.
items.title: Gammu before 1.45.2 Buffer Overflow via LoadBackup() MD5 Checksum

items.summary: Gammu before 1.45.2 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in ALCATEL_EncodeString() that allows attackers to overwrite stack memory via oversized encoded phonebook text. Attackers can supply a crafted backup restored with gammu restore or addnew to an attached Alcatel phone, using GSM extension characters to crash Gammu or potentially execute code.
items.title: Gammu before 1.45.2 Stack-Based Buffer Overflow via ALCATEL_EncodeString()

items.summary: Gammu before 1.45.2 contains a heap-based buffer overflow in ReadWAPSettingsEntry() that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory via crafted backup files with excess WAP or MMS settings entries. Attackers can supply a backup with more than four TitleNN keys in a [WAPSettings] or [MMSSettings] section, loaded via convertbackup, restore, or GSM_ReadBackupFile, causing crashes or potential code execution.
items.title: Gammu before 1.45.2 Heap Buffer Overflow via ReadWAPSettingsEntry()

items.summary: Gammu before 1.45.2 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in SaveBackupText() in backtext.c that allows attackers to corrupt stack memory by supplying long text fields. Attackers can craft a backup with long calendar or note fields that, when converted with gammu convertbackup, writes hex digits past the 10,000-byte stack buffer.
items.title: Gammu before 1.45.2 Stack-Based Buffer Overflow via SaveBackupText()

items.summary: HyperSpy from 1.2.0 before 2.6.0 contains a code execution vulnerability that allows attackers to run Python code by embedding malicious expression strings evaluated with sympy.sympify(). Attackers can craft .hspy or .zspy files with malicious axis, Expression component, or twin function expressions that execute when victims call hs.load() or restore models.
items.title: HyperSpy before 2.6.0 Code Execution via sympy.sympify() in HSPY/ZSPY Files

items.summary: HyperSpy from 1.4.0 before 2.6.0 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute arbitrary Python code by supplying crafted stored-model data in .hspy or .zspy files. Attackers can embed a malicious pickle payload in a component's _class_dump or a 'fn'-flagged _whitelist entry, which cloudpickle.loads() (dill in 1.x) runs when the victim restores the model.
items.title: HyperSpy 1.4.0 before 2.6.0 Insecure Deserialization RCE via Stored Model Restoration

items.summary: Kestra before 1.3.36 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute JavaScript by injecting HTML into the executions page sort parameter. Attackers can lure logged-in users to a crafted link whose invalid sort value is rendered unsanitized in an error toast, stealing the non-HttpOnly BASIC_AUTH credential cookie to take over the instance.
items.title: Kestra before 1.3.36 Reflected XSS via Executions Page Sort Parameter

items.summary: Kestra 1.3.24 before 2.0.0 contains a timing side-channel vulnerability in BasicAuthService.isAuthenticated() that allows unauthenticated attackers to enumerate the administrator username. Attackers can send Basic-auth requests with candidate usernames to protected API endpoints and detect slower bcrypt checks to identify the valid account for password guessing.
items.title: Kestra 1.3.24 before 2.0.0 Username Enumeration via Basic-Auth Timing

items.summary: Kestra 1.3.24 before 1.3.41 contains an insufficient credential expiration vulnerability that allows holders of a revoked administrator password to keep authenticating on peer webserver nodes through BasicAuthService's process-local verified-token cache. Attackers whose token remains cached on a peer node can call POST /api/v1/{tenant}/basicAuth to overwrite the shared administrator credentials and lock out the legitimate administrator.
items.title: Kestra 1.3.24 before 1.3.41 Insufficient Credential Expiration via Basic-Auth Token Cache

items.summary: ClassroomIO through 1.0.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated course members to access other tenants' newsfeed posts by supplying a foreign feedId under their own courseId. Attackers can read, react to, and comment on cross-organization posts, while team members or org admins can also overwrite content, pin flags, and delete them.
items.title: ClassroomIO through 1.0.0 IDOR via Course Newsfeed API Routes

items.summary: picomatch through 4.0.7 contains a glob filter bypass vulnerability because globstar (**) patterns are compiled without the dotAll flag and fail to match line terminators. Attackers who control file, object key or archive entry names containing newline characters can evade ** deny patterns, causing excluded resources to be included and exposed.
items.title: picomatch through 4.0.7 Glob Filter Bypass via Globstar Line Terminators

items.summary: FeatBit before 6.1.3 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated members of one organization to read other organizations' segments by supplying foreign segment identifiers. Attackers can query the SegmentController segment, by-ids, and flag-references endpoints with their own envId to retrieve end-user keys, targeting rules, and referencing feature flag keys.
items.title: FeatBit before 6.1.3 Authorization Bypass via SegmentController Segment Read Endpoints

items.summary: SimGear through 2024.1.7 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in sgSimpleBuffer::resize() where an unsigned 32-bit wraparound in the size-doubling loop leaves the size at zero. Attackers can supply a crafted .btg scenery file with an oversized byte count exceeding 2^31 to hang the loading process in FlightGear.
items.title: SimGear through 2024.1.7 Infinite Loop DoS via sgSimpleBuffer::resize()

items.summary: bgpq4 before 1.17 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in expander.c that allows malicious IRR servers to corrupt heap memory by sending crafted A<len> replies. Attackers controlling the IRR server or tampering with the plaintext TCP connection can announce a ULONG_MAX or -1 length, wrapping the allocation to one byte and crashing bgpq4.
items.title: bgpq4 before 1.17 Heap Buffer Overflow via IRRd A<len> Reply Handling

items.summary: Otter – Page Builder Blocks & Extensions for Gutenberg before 3.2.12 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows Contributor-level attackers to make the server contact arbitrary hosts via crafted Mailchimp API keys. Attackers can POST to the otter/v1/form/editor REST route with an apiKey whose data-center segment embeds a host, following redirects to internal services and reading partial responses.
items.title: Otter Blocks before 3.2.12 SSRF via Mailchimp API Key Validation

items.summary: Otter – Page Builder Blocks & Extensions for Gutenberg before 3.2.12 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in the Posts Grid block and Atomic Wind query loop that allows Contributor-level attackers to read non-public post type entries. Attackers can set the postTypes or queryPostType block attributes to types like flamingo_inbound or shop_coupon to expose titles and text, while the Atomic Wind custom_field path also leaks protected post meta.
items.title: Otter Blocks before 3.2.12 Incorrect Authorization via Posts Grid and Atomic Wind

items.summary: A flaw was found in GIMP. The Levels configuration setter does not validate the channel enum before using it to index fixed-size per-channel arrays. A crafted XCF file with a non-destructive Levels filter can set an out-of-range channel (LUMINANCE or RGB), causing a heap out-of-bounds read and write when the file is opened. This may lead to a crash or arbitrary code execution.
items.title: Gimp: gimp: heap out-of-bounds write via unvalidated levels channel property

items.summary: ntfy before v2.38.3 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows remote attackers to bypass the web push endpoint allow-list by crafting a URL containing '#' or '?' characters that satisfy the [^/]+ regex pattern used to validate mozaws.net and notify.windows.com hosts. Attackers can submit an endpoint .example#.mozaws.net/push, which passes validation while Go parses the actual host as attacker.example, causing the server to send subsequent web push POST requests to an attacker-controlled or internal host.
items.title: ntfy before 2.38.3 SSRF via Web Push Endpoint Allow-list Bypass

items.summary: Crypto APIs MCP server packages (@cryptoapis-io/mcp-*) before 0.4.0, mcp-blockchain-events, mcp-blockchain-fees, mcp-broadcast and mcp-prepare-transactions before 0.5.0, and mcp-aml before 0.2.0 contain a missing authentication vulnerability that allows unauthenticated network attackers to invoke tools using the operator's API key. When started with Streamable HTTP transport and --api-key, the server binds 0.0.0.0 and exposes /mcp, letting attackers consume paid credits, read account data, redirect event subscriptions, and delete HD wallet xPubs.
items.title: Crypto APIs MCP Servers (@cryptoapis-io/mcp-*) Missing Authentication via Streamable HTTP Transport

items.summary: Bagel (bagel-mcp) before 2.5.5 exposes unsandboxed DuckDB SQL execution through the read-only annotated query_messages MCP tool, allowing file access and network requests. Attackers who prompt-inject the driving LLM via recorded logs or topics can invoke read_csv_auto, COPY TO, or httpfs to read and write files and perform server-side request forgery.
items.title: Bagel before 2.5.5 Unsandboxed DuckDB SQL Execution via query_messages

items.summary: Bagel (bagel-mcp) before 2.5.5 contains an argument injection vulnerability in RsyncFilesToLocalDirectory that allows attackers to inject rsync options because only --quiet and --log-format values are rejected. Attackers who influence the LLM through prompt-injected content can trigger run_pipeline with -e/--rsh or --rsync-path options to execute commands as the Bagel server process.
items.title: Bagel before 2.5.5 Argument Injection via rsync Pipeline Task Options

items.summary: Wazuh-MCP-Server before commit 2bbfe12 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the blueteam_check_webshell tool because WebshellCheckInput.validate_url accepts DNS hostnames without resolving them. Attackers can supply URLs whose hostnames resolve or redirect to loopback, private, or link-local addresses, making curl reach internal services and cloud metadata endpoints and leak response details.
items.title: Wazuh-MCP-Server before commit 2bbfe12 SSRF via blueteam_check_webshell Hostname Bypass

items.summary: SylphxAI pdf-reader-mcp 2.4.1 through 3.0.14, 3.0.16, and 3.1.2 through 3.1.4 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in its PDF URL loader, which validates the resolved address but does not pin it for fetch(). Attackers controlling DNS for a url passed to read_pdf can return a public address at check time and an internal address at connection time to reach internal services and cloud metadata endpoints.
items.title: SylphxAI pdf-reader-mcp 2.4.1 through 3.1.4 SSRF via DNS Rebinding in URL Loader

items.summary: Typebot from 2.14.0 before 3.19.0 contains an authorization flaw that allows authenticated bot authors to reference another workspace's legacy webhook by saving a foreign webhookId in an HTTP request block. Attackers can have executeHttpRequestBlock return the victim's URL, headers and body client-side, or use handleSubscribeHttpRequest to overwrite the victim's webhook URL and redirect its data.
items.title: Typebot from 2.14.0 before 3.19.0 Cross-Workspace Webhook Disclosure via Unscoped webhookId

items.summary: WhoDB from 0.88.0 before 0.132.0 contains an access control bypass in the MCP whodb_query tool, letting callers run file-writing statements without approval because the sqlguard keyword classifier omits INTO, OUTFILE and DUMPFILE. MCP clients or prompt-injected models can execute PostgreSQL lo_export or MySQL SELECT INTO OUTFILE to create files on the database host and create tables, bypassing confirmation and read-only modes.
items.title: WhoDB 0.88.0 before 0.132.0 MCP Read-Only Bypass via Server-Side File Writes

items.summary: mcp-video-analyzer 0.2.0 before 0.10.1 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows attackers to reach internal addresses by supplying any http(s) URL ending in a video extension. Attackers can use prompt injection to make tools like get_frames fetch loopback, private, or cloud metadata addresses directly or via redirects, writing responses to disk or returning rendered screenshots.
items.title: mcp-video-analyzer 0.2.0 before 0.10.1 SSRF via Direct Video URLs

items.summary: bigcommerce-api-mcp before 1.0.1 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to invoke MCP tools because the /sse and /messages routes skip the authenticateRequest middleware. Attackers can open /sse to obtain a session id and POST JSON-RPC tool calls to /messages to retrieve store product, order and customer records using the operator's BigCommerce API key.
items.title: bigcommerce-api-mcp before 1.0.1 Missing Authentication via SSE Transport Routes

items.summary: smalot/pdfparser before 2.14.0 contains an inefficient algorithmic complexity vulnerability that allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service by submitting a crafted PDF with deeply nested unbalanced parentheses in a content-stream string. Attackers can exploit the regex-based string isolation loop in PDFObject::formatContent(), which rescans growing content on each pass to produce O(n^2) processing time, causing a small PDF to stall or exhaust PHP worker resources for seconds to minutes.
items.title: smalot/pdfparser before 2.14.0 Quadratic-Time DoS via formatContent()

items.summary: A security flaw has been discovered in eosphoros-ai DB-GPT up to 0.8.3. This affects the function editor_sql_run of the file packages/dbgpt-app/src/dbgpt_app/openapi/api_v1/editor/api_editor_v1.py of the component Editor SQL Run API. Performing a manipulation of the argument db_name results in authorization bypass. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.
items.title: eosphoros-ai DB-GPT Editor SQL Run API api_editor_v1.py editor_sql_run authorization

items.summary: libexpat through 2.11.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability in defineAttribute() of lib/xmlparse.c that fails to detect duplicate non-ID #IMPLIED or #REQUIRED attribute declarations. Attackers can supply a crafted XML document with repeated ATTLIST declarations in an internal DTD subset to cause quadratic CPU consumption in storeAtts() during parsing.
items.title: libexpat through 2.11.0 Denial of Service via defineAttribute Duplicate Declarations

items.summary: Leo through 6.8.10 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute code by embedding pickled data in unknown XML attributes of .leo outlines. Attackers can place a pickle __reduce__ gadget in a <t> or <v> element attribute that resolveUa passes to pickle.loads, executing code with user privileges when the outline is opened.
items.title: Leo through 6.8.10 Insecure Deserialization RCE via .leo Outline Attributes

items.summary: FOG Project before 1.6.0.119 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain host tokens from status/hostgetkey.php by supplying a host MAC address. Attackers can present the token to service/hostinfo.php to retrieve decrypted Active Directory join credentials and Windows product keys during deployment windows.
items.title: FOG Project before 1.6.0.119 Credential Disclosure via status/hostgetkey.php Token Endpoint

items.summary: Zettlr before 4.11.0 fails to validate URI schemes in Markdown link targets, allowing attackers to launch arbitrary registered protocol handlers via Electron shell.openExternal without confirmation. Attackers can craft documents whose Ctrl/Cmd-clicked links use smb:// to leak NTLM credential hashes on Windows or invoke custom protocol handlers with attacker-controlled parameters.
items.title: Zettlr before 4.11.0 Unvalidated URI Scheme Handling via Markdown Links

items.summary: HCIPy through 0.7.1 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute code by supplying crafted .pkl files to read_field, read_grid or read_mode_basis. Because hcipy/util/io.py selects pickle by file extension and calls pickle.load, a __reduce__ gadget in a pupil, apodizer, PSF or mode-basis file runs code with the user's privileges.
items.title: HCIPy through 0.7.1 Insecure Deserialization via Pickle Files in io.py

items.summary: Detoxify 0.5.3 through 0.5.4 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability in load_checkpoint that allows attackers to execute code by supplying a crafted checkpoint file. Attackers can embed a pickle __reduce__ gadget in a .ckpt file loaded via torch.load with weights_only=False to run code with the user's privileges.
items.title: Detoxify 0.5.3 through 0.5.4 Insecure Deserialization RCE via load_checkpoint

items.summary: JSONSchema2PoPo2 through 3.0.3 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows attackers to inject Python code by supplying JSON Schema default or format values that are written unescaped. Attackers can place a single quote in a string property default to break out of the literal in the generated __init__ signature, executing injected code when the generated module is imported.
items.title: JSONSchema2PoPo2 through 3.0.3 Code Injection via python_class.tmpl Template

items.summary:
dns_resolve_cancel_with_name() in subsys/net/lib/dns/resolve.c looks up the pending query to cancel by DNS id plus a hash of the name the caller originally asked for. When a reply contains only a CNAME, the resolver sends a new query for the alias and overwrites the slot's query_hash with the hash of the alias name. After one or more CNAME hops, cancelling by the original name silently fails with -ENOENT and the query stays pending.

zsock_getaddrinfo() (exec_query() in subsys/net/lib/sockets/getaddrinfo.c) passes a pointer to its stack-local ai_state as the resolver callback context. When its semaphore wait times out, it calls dns_cancel_addr_info_with_name(), ignores the result, and returns. The CNAME re-query restarts the resolver timer, so a CNAME-only response that arrives more than about 100 ms after the query lets the getaddrinfo() wait expire first. The cancel then fails and getaddrinfo() returns. An attacker who can supply DNS responses can trigger this reliably: a malicious or compromised DNS server, an on-path attacker, or any host on the link for mDNS/LLMNR lookups. The device only has to resolve a name with getaddrinfo().

When the orphaned query later times out, dns_resolve_cb() writes the status and calls k_sem_give() on the dead stack frame. If the attacker answers the alias query instead, the callback copies attacker-supplied address data through a stale ai_arr pointer read from the reused stack. The result is a kernel fault (denial of service) or memory corruption in the calling thread's stack and whatever memory the stale pointer references.
items.title: Use-after-return in getaddrinfo() when a DNS query that followed a CNAME cannot be cancelled

items.summary:
The system call verifier z_vrfy_k_thread_stack_space_get() in kernel/thread.c checked the result of K_SYSCALL_OBJ(thread, K_OBJ_THREAD) with the CHECKIF() macro instead of K_OOPS(). CHECKIF() compiles to if (0) when CONFIG_NO_RUNTIME_CHECKS is selected, and becomes an assertion when CONFIG_ASSERT_ON_ERRORS is selected. In both cases, the kernel-object validation result for the user-supplied thread pointer is ignored, or is a no-op when assertions are disabled.

On builds with CONFIG_USERSPACE, CONFIG_INIT_STACKS and CONFIG_THREAD_STACK_INFO plus one of those check modes, a user-mode thread can call k_thread_stack_space_get() with an arbitrary pointer. That pointer can be a fake struct k_thread in its own memory, or a thread object it has no permission on. z_impl_k_thread_stack_space_get() then dereferences thread->stack_info in supervisor mode and scans memory starting at the attacker-chosen stack_info.start.

The syscall returns the number of leading 0xAA bytes at that address. This gives an unprivileged thread a limited oracle on arbitrary kernel or peripheral memory, and allows privileged reads of attacker-selected addresses, including MMIO. No write primitive results. The default CONFIG_RUNTIME_ERROR_CHECKS configuration is not affected. The fix replaces the CHECKIF() with K_OOPS() so the object check is always enforced.
items.title: Kernel object validation bypass in k_thread_stack_space_get syscall verifier with CONFIG_NO_RUNTIME_CHECKS

items.summary:
The MCUmgr SMP client matched an incoming response to a pending command in smp_client_response_discover() (subsys/mgmt/mcumgr/smp_client/src/client.c) using only the 8-bit sequence number and the operation. It did not check the transport the response arrived on, or the group and command ID. smp_process_request_packet() hands every MGMT_OP_READ_RSP/MGMT_OP_WRITE_RSP packet received on any SMP transport to smp_client_single_response(), so a response from any SMP peer could complete any pending client command.

On a device that is both an SMP server (for example over Bluetooth LE or UDP) and an SMP client (CONFIG_SMP_CLIENT, for example using img_mgmt_client to update a companion MCU over UART), a peer on the server transport can send up to 256 forged response packets while a client operation is pending and have one of them accepted as the reply from the managed device. Non-matching responses are dropped silently. The response path bypasses the server command handlers, so restricting which server groups a peer may use does not prevent it.

The attacker can forge the results of client operations. For example, a forged image-upload offset makes img_mgmt_client_upload() report success after only part of the image was sent, a forged image-state response can report arbitrary versions or flags, and any pending command can be forced to fail. No memory corruption results: the response callbacks bound-check the decoded data. The target's own image validation limits the result to failed or suppressed updates and disrupted management operations. The fix restricts matching to commands sent on the same transport with the same group and command ID. Responses from a different peer on the same transport are still not distinguished.
items.title: MCUmgr SMP client accepts responses from any transport, allowing spoofed command results

items.summary: Nmap before 7.992 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in DNS::ResolverImpl::handle_write in libnetutil/massdns.cc that dereferences freed request objects after writes complete. Attackers controlling or on-path to a DNS server can send timed DNS responses with forged ICMP port-unreachable messages to crash scans, disclose memory, or hijack execution.
items.title: Nmap before 7.992 Use-After-Free via DNS Resolver handle_write

items.summary: Nmap before 7.992 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in DNS::ResolverImpl::process_request in libnetutil/massdns.cc that frees still-referenced requests when rescheduling after DNS server disconnects. Attackers answering for at least two configured DNS servers can force a disconnect and send a precisely timed response to crash the scan, possibly enabling code execution.
items.title: Nmap before 7.992 Use-After-Free via Parallel DNS Resolver process_request

items.summary: Nmap before 7.992 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the Nmap Scripting Engine because nse_main.lua does not explicitly seed Lua's math.random generator. Malicious scanned hosts can observe math.random-derived values in NSE script traffic during -sC scans, brute-force the seed, and recover a heap address that weakens ASLR.
items.title: Nmap before 7.992 Heap Address Disclosure via Predictable NSE Lua Seed

items.summary: libexpat 2.6.0 through 2.11.0 built with XML_GE=0 and XML_UNICODE contains an out-of-bounds read in storeSelfEntityValue() because narrow string literals are treated as wide strings. Attackers can supply an XML document whose DOCTYPE declares a general entity to expose adjacent static memory through the entity value or crash the parser.
items.title: libexpat 2.6.0 through 2.11.0 Out-of-Bounds Read via storeSelfEntityValue

items.summary: svglib before 2.5.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability in SvgRenderer.renderNode() that recursively renders internal <image> href fragment references without expansion limits or cycle detection. Attackers can supply crafted SVGs to svg2rlg() with nested groups referencing each other twice or self-referencing images to cause exponential resource consumption or RecursionError crashes.
items.title: svglib before 2.5.0 Denial of Service via Recursive Image Fragment References

items.summary: Pydantic Deep 0.2.18 before 0.4.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the bundled DeepResearch FastAPI app that exposes HTTP routes and the /ws/chat WebSocket. Remote attackers reaching the server bound to all interfaces can enumerate sessions, read event logs and workspace files, drive the research agent, and delete sessions.
items.title: Pydantic Deep 0.2.18 before 0.4.0 Missing Authentication in DeepResearch App

items.summary: Pydantic Deep 0.2.18 before 0.4.0 contains a server-side request forgery and local file read vulnerability in the DeepResearch export_report handler for /export/pdf. Attackers can inject raw HTML into reports via the unauthenticated /upload endpoint, causing WeasyPrint to fetch internal URLs and embed local server files into exported PDFs.
items.title: Pydantic Deep 0.2.18 before 0.4.0 SSRF and File Read via /export/pdf

items.summary: PlantUML through 1.2026.10, including PlantUML Server, contains a local file read vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass SANDBOX and INTERNET security profiles via Graphviz node attributes. Attackers can submit @startdot diagrams with image or shapefile attributes to render local image files into PNG output and probe whether arbitrary local paths exist.
items.title: PlantUML through 1.2026.10 Local File Read via @startdot Graphviz Image Attribute

items.summary: AVideo from 29.1.0 before 29.8.0 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in plugin/YPTWallet/view/saveConfiguration.php that lets attackers modify a logged-in user's wallet configuration. Attackers can lure victims to a page auto-submitting a cross-origin POST with CryptoWallet and donation_notification_url to redirect payouts and capture donation notifications.
items.title: AVideo from 29.1.0 before 29.8.0 CSRF via YPTWallet saveConfiguration.php

items.summary: n8n before 1.123.96, 2.47.6, 2.48.3, and 3.2.2 contains a path traversal vulnerability in integration nodes that build API request paths from unencoded record, table, or resource ID parameters. Attackers can supply relative path segments through untrusted input such as webhook bodies to read, modify, or delete unintended resources using the node's stored credential.
items.title: n8n before 1.123.96, 2.47.6, 2.48.3, and 3.2.2 Path Traversal in Integration Nodes

items.summary: n8n before 2.47.6, 2.48.x before 2.48.3, and 3.x before 3.2.2 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the AWS Bedrock Chat Model and Embeddings AWS Bedrock nodes, where requests to a custom Bedrock runtime endpoint set in an AWS credential bypass n8n's SSRF protection. An authenticated user who can create AWS credentials can point the endpoint at internal or blocked addresses, causing n8n to send requests there and exposing the start of responses in node errors.
items.title: n8n before 2.47.6, 2.48.3, and 3.2.2 SSRF via AWS Bedrock Custom Runtime Endpoint

items.summary: n8n before 1.123.96, 2.x before 2.47.6, 2.48.x before 2.48.3, and 3.x before 3.2.2 does not verify that the user activating a workflow can access the credentials set on its trigger nodes. An authenticated member who knows another user's credential ID can activate a workflow whose trigger uses it, causing n8n to create or delete webhooks on the connected service with that credential's privileges and deliver events from attacker-chosen resources to the member's workflow.
items.title: n8n before 1.123.96, 2.47.6, 2.48.3, and 3.2.2 Improper Authorization in Workflow Activation Trigger Credentials

items.summary: Budibase backend-core before 3.49.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated Builder/Creator users to bypass the outbound-fetch deny list by targeting the IPv6 unspecified address. Attackers can supply URLs with host [::] to features like Outgoing Webhook or REST datasources to reach IPv6 loopback services and read reflected internal responses.
items.title: Budibase backend-core before 3.49.0 SSRF via IPv6 Unspecified Address Bypass

items.summary: Budibase before 3.51.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the workspace create handler that allows authenticated CREATOR users to probe server paths by supplying an unvalidated body.file.path value. Attackers can enumerate filesystem existence and type, and for directories containing db.txt, copy contents into their object store namespace before the directory is recursively deleted.
items.title: Budibase before 3.51.0 Filesystem Oracle and Directory Deletion via body.file.path

items.summary: Budibase server before 3.48.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the public API view row search endpoint that skips per-view permission checks due to a tableId/viewId parameter mismatch. Authenticated users with READ_ONLY role and an API key can query restricted views to read data limited to higher-privileged roles.
items.title: Budibase Server before 3.48.0 Authorization Bypass via Public API View Search

items.summary: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a hard-coded credentials vulnerability where the Helm chart values.yaml sets secret_key_base and lockbox_key to a static published constant. Unauthenticated attackers can sign session tokens with the known key to impersonate any user and decrypt all stored datasource credentials.
items.title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS Hard-Coded JWT and Encryption Keys in Helm Chart

items.summary: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a command injection vulnerability in its GitHub Actions release workflow, which interpolates the pull request title directly into a shell run block. Attackers can submit a pull request against a release branch with shell metacharacters in its title that, once merged, executes commands with a cross-repository GITHUB_TOKEN, enabling unauthorized merges into enterprise repositories.
items.title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS Command Injection via Release Workflow Pull Request Title

items.summary: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated users with the TEST_CONNECTION ability to reach arbitrary hosts by supplying body-controlled datasource options. Attackers can set kind, plugin_id, and host options for plugins like influxdb or elasticsearch to reach loopback, internal services, or cloud metadata endpoints exposing IAM credentials.
items.title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS SSRF via Data Source test-connection Endpoint

items.summary: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an arbitrary file read and SSRF vulnerability in the SMTP plugin that allows authenticated app builders to pass object values to Nodemailer. Attackers can set textContent or htmlContent to path or href content objects to email server files or internal cloud metadata responses to themselves.
items.title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS SMTP Plugin Arbitrary File Read and SSRF

items.summary: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated users to make the server fetch internal URLs via the gRPC v2 proto_file_url option. Attackers can target loopback, private, cloud metadata, or redirect-controlled addresses, or serve oversized responses that are buffered and parsed synchronously, causing denial of service.
items.title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS SSRF via gRPC v2 proto_file_url Import

items.summary: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the OAuth token exchange for custom datasources, which sends requests to an unvalidated, user-configured access_token_url. Authenticated users can trigger the authorize_oauth2 endpoint to reach loopback, cloud metadata, or private network services, with internal response bodies reflected in some API error responses.
items.title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS SSRF via OAuth access_token_url Token Exchange

items.summary: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a server-side request forgery protection bypass because getSSRFProtectionOptions passes its safe resolver as dnsLookup instead of lookup. Attackers controlling datasource hostnames can use DNS rebinding in REST API, GraphQL, OpenAPI, or OAuth requests to reach blocked private addresses.
items.title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS SSRF Protection Bypass via DNS Rebinding

items.summary: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in ssrf-protection.ts that fails to classify NAT64 (64:ff9b::/96, 64:ff9b:1::/48) and 6to4 (2002::/16) IPv6 addresses embedding internal IPv4. Authenticated users can set REST API, GraphQL, OpenAPI, or OAuth data-source URLs to attacker hostnames whose AAAA records resolve to these forms, bypassing pre-request and dial-time guards to reach cloud metadata and internal hosts.
items.title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS SSRF Protection Bypass via IPv6 NAT64/6to4 Addresses

items.summary: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the n8n, nocodb, baserow, couchdb, elasticsearch, influxdb, and databricks datasource plugins, which skip the validateUrlForSSRF check. Authenticated builders, or unauthenticated visitors of public apps with templated URLs, can supply internal URLs or hosts to read cloud metadata credentials and internal service responses.
items.title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS SSRF via Unprotected Datasource Plugins

items.summary: Heym before 0.0.154 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the workflow execute endpoint: anonymous workflows run as any signed-in caller, without an access check, using that caller's credentials and global variables. Authenticated attackers can lure signed-in users to a GET execute link for an attacker-owned anonymous workflow, which the SameSite=Lax session cookie authenticates. The attacker then reads the victim's decrypted credentials from the workflow's run history.
items.title: Heym before 0.0.154 Credential Theft via Anonymous Workflow Execute Endpoint

items.summary: Heym from 0.0.95 before 0.0.154 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to run script on the application origin by publishing HTML output mapper workflows. Attackers can set a workflow to anonymous GET and share the /api/workflows/{id}/execute link, causing visitors' browsers to send authenticated API requests to read or modify their workflows, credentials, and settings.
items.title: Heym 0.0.95 before 0.0.154 Stored XSS via htmlOutputMapper Workflows

items.summary: Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.19 and 1.7.x before 1.7.4 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in compose_part_body() in program/actions/mail/compose.php, which converts a text/enriched message part to HTML for the HTML editor without sanitizing the result. Attackers can send a crafted email with a text/enriched part so that script injected into the HTML editor runs in the victim's session when the victim replies to, forwards, or edits the message.
items.title: Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.19 and 1.7.x before 1.7.4 XSS in HTML Editor via text/enriched Content

items.summary: Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.19 and 1.7.x before 1.7.4 contains an authorization bypass in add_to_group() and remove_from_group() in program/lib/Roundcube/rcube_contacts.php, which did not verify that the contact group and the contacts belong to the current user. An authenticated user of the SQL address book can supply other users' group and contact identifiers to add contacts to or remove them from other users' contact groups, or to add other users' contacts to their own groups.
items.title: Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.19 and 1.7.x before 1.7.4 Cross-User Contact Group Membership Access

items.summary: Payload 3.25.0 before 3.90.0 and 4.0.0-canary.0 before 4.0.0-canary.34 contains an authorization bypass through a user-controlled key in its client upload handling, which used the upload collection supplied by the client instead of the one selected by the server. In deployments that use client uploads across multiple upload collections, an authenticated user with upload permissions can access files outside their authorized collection.
items.title: Payload 3.25.0 before 3.90.0 Authorization Bypass via Client Upload Collection

items.summary: PDFio before 1.6.5 contains an integer underflow in _pdfioCryptoAESDecrypt() in pdfio-aes.c, which strips PKCS#7 padding before any AES block has been decrypted when an AES-encrypted string or binary value holds only its 16-byte IV. Attackers can supply a crafted AES-encrypted PDF that, when opened with pdfioFileOpen(), makes the decrypted length underflow so that _pdfioValueDecrypt() reads and writes out of bounds, crashing the application or corrupting heap memory.
items.title: PDFio before 1.6.5 Out-of-Bounds Read/Write via IV-Only AES-Encrypted Strings

items.summary: Sparkle before 2.9.6 contains a time-of-check time-of-use race condition in the installer's SPUInstallationData handling in AppInstaller.m, which validates the symlink-resolved download URL but performs the privileged move on the unresolved URL and checks the file type only afterwards. A local user can swap an intermediate directory of the download path for a symlink between the check and the move, causing a root installer to rename a file out of a protected location and leading to privilege escalation when the installer runs in the system domain.
items.title: Sparkle before 2.9.6 Local Privilege Escalation via Installer Download Path Race

items.summary: Sparkle 2.2.0 before 2.9.6 contains a link following vulnerability in -submitInstallerAtPath: in SUInstallerLauncher.m that builds a root updater's launcher cache path inside the console user's home directory and then deletes and creates items there without rejecting symbolic links. A local console user can pre-create that path as a symlink while a CLI tool or daemon updates a bundle as root, making root delete old files in a directory of the attacker's choosing and create a directory there that is chowned to the attacker, leading to privilege escalation.
items.title: Sparkle 2.2.0 before 2.9.6 Local Privilege Escalation via Root Launcher Cache Symlink

items.summary: A flaw has been found in Free5GC 4.3.0. This vulnerability affects unknown code of the component SMF. This manipulation causes resource consumption. The attack may be initiated remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.
items.title: Free5GC SMF resource consumption

items.summary: FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in xwd_encode_frame() in libavcodec/xwdenc.c that copies each RGB24 or BGR24 row using the padded XWD scanline size instead of the pixel row size. Attackers who control the width of video encoded to XWD by an application that supplies tightly packed frames can make the encoder read past the frame buffer, crashing the application or leaking heap contents into the output image.
items.title: FFmpeg before 9.1 Out-of-Bounds Read via XWD Encoder Scanline Padding

items.summary: FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in pcx_encode_frame() in libavcodec/pcxenc.c that rounds each row up to an even number of bytes and run-length encodes that many bytes from the input frame. Attackers who control the width of images encoded to PCX by an application that supplies tightly packed frames can make the encoder read past the end of the frame buffer, crashing the application or leaking heap contents into the output image.
items.title: FFmpeg before 9.1 Out-of-Bounds Read via PCX Encoder Odd-Width Rows

items.summary: FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in xsub_encode() in libavcodec/xsubenc.c that only warns when a subtitle has no rectangles and then dereferences rects[0]. Attackers can supply crafted PGS or DVB subtitles that decode to empty subtitle events, crashing applications that pass decoded subtitles directly to the XSUB encoder.
items.title: FFmpeg before 9.1 NULL Pointer Dereference via XSUB Encoder Empty Subtitles

items.summary: FFmpeg 7.1 before 9.1 contains a memory leak vulnerability in eb_receive_packet() in libavcodec/libsvtav1.c that returns without unreferencing the queued input frame when eb_send_frame() fails. Attackers can supply crafted video in which some frames lack Dolby Vision metadata to an SVT-AV1 encode with Dolby Vision RPU coding enabled, leaking each rejected frame's buffers or aborting in av_frame_move_ref() in builds with assertions enabled.
items.title: FFmpeg 7.1 before 9.1 Memory Leak via libsvtav1 Dolby Vision Encoding

items.summary: FFmpeg 3.0 before 8.1.3 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in libavfilter/vf_boxblur.c because query_formats() accepts pixel formats deeper than 16 bits while the blur temporary buffers hold only 2 bytes per pixel. Attackers can supply crafted 32-bit float media, such as PFM or OpenEXR images, that when processed by the boxblur filter overflow the temporary buffers, crashing applications or possibly executing code.
items.title: FFmpeg 3.0 before 8.1.3 Heap Buffer Overflow via boxblur Filter

items.summary: FFmpeg 5.0 before 8.1.3 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in the IMF demuxer in libavformat/imfdec.c because open_virtual_track() accepts a virtual track with no resources. Attackers can supply a crafted IMF Composition Playlist whose virtual track lists no resources, causing set_context_streams_from_tracks() to dereference a NULL resource array and crash the process.
items.title: FFmpeg 5.0 before 8.1.3 NULL Pointer Dereference via IMF Virtual Track Without Resources

items.summary: FFmpeg 5.0 before 8.1.3 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in parse_imf_asset_map_from_xml_dom() in libavformat/imfdec.c that does not check for a missing or empty Path element in an asset map Chunk. Attackers can supply a crafted IMF ASSETMAP.xml whose Chunk lacks a Path, passing a NULL URI to the path handling functions and crashing the process.
items.title: FFmpeg 5.0 before 8.1.3 NULL Pointer Dereference via IMF Asset Map Missing Path

items.summary: A security flaw has been discovered in Free5GC up to 4.2.3. Affected is the function handleAssociationSetupRequest of the file internal/pfcp/association.go of the component UPF. Performing a manipulation results in missing authentication. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure.
items.title: Free5GC UPF association.go handleAssociationSetupRequest missing authentication

items.summary: A vulnerability was identified in eosphoros-ai DB-GPT up to 0.8.3. The impacted element is the function get_editor_tables of the file packages/dbgpt-app/src/dbgpt_app/openapi/api_v1/editor/api_editor_v1.py of the component Editor API. Such manipulation of the argument db_name leads to improper access controls. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure.
items.title: eosphoros-ai DB-GPT Editor API api_editor_v1.py get_editor_tables access control

items.summary: A vulnerability was detected in ONNX ONNXMLTools up to 1.16.0. This affects the function get_set_node of the file onnxmltools/utils/visualize.py of the component Model Visualization. The manipulation results in cross site scripting. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.
items.title: ONNX ONNXMLTools Model Visualization visualize.py get_set_node cross site scripting

items.summary: A vulnerability was identified in RT-Thread up to 5.3.0. This impacts the function hpm_adc_enabled of the file bsp/hpmicro/libraries/drivers/drv_adc.c of the component HPM ADC Driver. The manipulation of the argument channel leads to improper validation of array index. The attack needs to be performed locally. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The identifier of the patch is fc64f78669b42b35981f97c23c7e952832f3b48b. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue.
items.title: RT-Thread HPM ADC Driver drv_adc.c hpm_adc_enabled array index

items.summary: lastversion before 3.6.20 contains a path traversal vulnerability in extract_tar() that allows attackers to write files outside the extraction directory via tar symlink members. Attackers controlling a project's release assets can craft a tarball with a symlink followed by a file beneath it, writing files like usercustomize.py to achieve code execution.
items.title: lastversion before 3.6.20 Arbitrary File Write via Tar Symlink Members

items.summary: InternLM LMDeploy 0.9.0 through 0.18.0 contains an unbounded resource allocation vulnerability in the DistServe proxy /distserve/connection_warmup endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust memory. While a prefill/decode connection is pending, for example after registering a slow node via /nodes/add, repeated warmup requests spawn unbounded wait_for_conn() tasks and sockets until the proxy process is killed.
items.title: InternLM LMDeploy 0.9.0 through 0.18.0 Memory Exhaustion via /distserve/connection_warmup

items.summary: A security flaw has been discovered in Tencent RapidJSON up to 1.1.0. This affects the function Writer::WriteString in the library include/rapidjson/writer.h. Performing a manipulation of the argument length results in integer overflow. The attack may be initiated remotely. The patch is named 297637bc0a0f00dc504dbc1a47ebdaa577f8ae19. To fix this issue, it is recommended to deploy a patch.
items.title: Tencent RapidJSON writer.h WriteString integer overflow

items.summary: FreeRDP before 3.33.0 contains a race condition in asynchronous RDPDR IRP processing that allows malicious RDP servers to leak client memory through non-atomic wStream reference count updates. Attackers can send repeated IRPs, such as smartcard redirection requests, so concurrent Stream_Release() calls lose decrements and accumulate unreleased streams, exhausting memory and causing denial of service.
items.title: FreeRDP before 3.33.0 Memory Leak via Non-Atomic RDPDR IRP Stream Refcount

items.summary: FreeRDP from 3.0.0 before 3.33.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the shadow server's fast-path input handlers in fastpath.c that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject input before activation. Attackers can negotiate TLS-only RDP, skip Confirm Active, and send Fast-Path Input Event PDUs to inject keystrokes and mouse movement into the host X11 session via XTEST.
items.title: FreeRDP 3.0.0 before 3.33.0 Missing Authentication via Fast-Path Input PDUs

items.summary: FreeRDP from 3.0.0 before 3.33.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in cert_write_server_certificate_v1() that computes the proprietary certificate signature over a freed stream buffer after reallocation. Clients negotiating Standard RDP Security with many static channels against servers using 3072- or 4096-bit keys trigger freed heap reads, producing invalid certificate signatures.
items.title: FreeRDP 3.0.0 before 3.33.0 Use-After-Free in Server Certificate Signing

items.summary: Parse Server before 9.12.0-alpha.2 matches $in, $nin, $all and $containedBy constraints in LiveQuery with a cost proportional to the product of the constraint list size and the saved array size. A client that can subscribe to a class and save objects in it can use large lists and arrays to block the event loop for seconds or longer, stalling LiveQuery and, when it runs in the same process, Parse Server.
items.title: Parse Server before 9.12.0-alpha.2 LiveQuery Denial of Service via List Constraints

items.summary: SiYuan before 3.8.11 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject DOM event handlers by storing handler-named block attributes such as onmouseover. Attackers can share crafted .sy.zip packages or Markdown files whose attributes reach renderCustom or the unsanitised preview pane, executing OS commands via Node integration in the desktop app.
items.title: SiYuan before 3.8.11 Stored XSS to RCE via Block Attribute Names

items.summary: vLLM 0.21.0 before 0.28.0, when using the V1 model runner, contains a state aliasing flaw in ThinkingBudgetStateHolder.sync_batch(), whose SWAP branch copies thinking-budget state to the destination batch row without removing the source entry. Attackers submitting requests with thinking_token_budget can force the reasoning-end token sequence into a concurrent co-batched request's output during a mixed batch reorder.
items.title: vLLM 0.21.0 before 0.28.0 Cross-Request State Aliasing via thinking_token_budget

items.summary: Traefik 3.1.0 before 3.7.18 and 3.8.0-rc.1 contain a memory exhaustion vulnerability in the Compress middleware, which creates zstd encoders with library default options that retain about 18 MiB of state per response until it is fully written. Unauthenticated remote attackers can open many concurrent requests and read responses slowly to exhaust memory and crash Traefik.
items.title: Traefik from 3.1.0 before 3.7.18 Memory Exhaustion DoS via Compress Middleware

items.summary: Hono from 4.12.16 before 4.13.18 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability in the bodyLimit() middleware that retains every transfer chunk as a separate array. Unauthenticated attackers can send a within-limit request body in one-byte chunks to create millions of retained objects, terminating Bun or Node.js processes.
items.title: Hono 4.12.16 before 4.13.18 Memory Exhaustion via bodyLimit() Middleware

items.summary: SurrealDB before 4.0.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read SELECT-hidden edge endpoints through InOverride/OutOverride error messages. Attackers with CREATE and UPDATE permission on an edge table can re-RELATE an existing edge with mismatched endpoints to recover stored in/out record ids despite row- or field-level restrictions.
items.title: SurrealDB before 4.0.0 Information Disclosure via RELATE Endpoint Override Errors

items.summary: Budibase server from 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows view users and anonymous visitors to access entire base tables by passing a view id to the /api/:viewId/rows routes. Attackers can read, export, modify, and delete rows outside the view filter, including hidden columns, or read the full table unauthenticated through PUBLIC views.
items.title: Budibase from 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 Authorization Bypass via View Row Routes

items.summary: Budibase before 4.0.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to retrieve legacy LiteLLM credentials by querying the public settings endpoint. Attackers can send unauthenticated GET requests to /api/global/configs/public to obtain liteLLM.keyId and secretKey, enabling unauthorized use of tenant LiteLLM resources.
items.title: Budibase before 4.0.0 Information Disclosure via /api/global/configs/public

items.summary: Budibase before 4.0.0 contains a JSON injection vulnerability that allows attackers to inject JSON structure into S3 delete and Google Sheets row fields via unescaped template parameters. Attackers can submit crafted parameters to the queries endpoint to add extra Key entries, deleting chosen S3 objects or overriding Sheets row columns.
items.title: Budibase before 4.0.0 JSON Injection via S3 Delete and Google Sheets Query Fields

items.summary: Scriban before 7.6.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability that allows template authors to bypass LimitToString by rendering a ScriptObject with many members. Attackers can supply a small template whose ScriptObject.ToString concatenates large member values without length tracking, allocating multi-gigabyte strings and causing memory exhaustion.
items.title: Scriban before 7.6.0 LimitToString Bypass via ScriptObject String Conversion

items.summary: Nodemailer 9.1.0 before 10.4.1 lowercases recipient domains with JavaScript toLowerCase() in _normalizeAddress before UTS-46 mapping, which converts U+1E9E and word-final U+03A3 differently than WHATWG/UTS-46 validators. An unprivileged attacker can submit an address an application's allow-list approves, causing invites or shared links to reach an attacker-registered domain.
items.title: Nodemailer 9.1.0 before 10.4.1 IDN Allow-List Bypass via toLowerCase() Domain Normalization

items.summary: ToolJet before 3.21.94-beta contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows Builders with only data source Delete permission to update global data sources via the PUT /api/data-sources endpoint. Attackers can change a REST data source base URL so later query executions send stored Bearer credentials to an attacker-controlled endpoint.
items.title: ToolJet before 3.21.94-beta Improper Authorization in Data Source Update

items.summary: ToolJet from 3.20.84 before 3.21.96-LTS contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the instance-level SSO sign-in path that hardcodes signup as enabled, ignoring all signup-disable controls. Any user with an account on the configured GitHub or Google identity provider can sign in via the OAuth endpoint to obtain an admin session in a newly created workspace.
items.title: ToolJet 3.20.84 before 3.21.96-LTS Signup Control Bypass via Instance-Level SSO

items.summary: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated same-organization users to invoke OAuth2 authorization on data sources they cannot configure. Attackers can send POST requests to /api/data-sources/:id/authorize_oauth2 to bind attacker-controlled OAuth credentials or overwrite token state for foreign data sources.
items.title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS Authorization Bypass via authorize_oauth2 Data Source Route

items.summary: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated low-privilege users to recover plaintext workspace secret constants through OAuth URL generation. Attackers can send POST /api/data-sources/fetch-oauth2-base-url with {{secrets.*}} in source_options and arbitrary organization_id and environment_id to receive secrets, including other workspaces' secrets, in the returned authorization URL.
items.title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS Secret Disclosure via fetch-oauth2-base-url

items.summary: Tornado before 6.6.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in StaticFileHandler on Windows that allows unauthenticated attackers to read NTFS Alternate Data Streams by appending :streamname to URL paths. Attackers can request stream paths that pass the get_absolute_path and _check_in_root prefix checks to read hidden stream content, such as stored secrets or Zone.Identifier source data.
items.title: Tornado before 6.6.1 NTFS Alternate Data Stream Disclosure via StaticFileHandler

items.summary: Coder 2.9.0 before 2.29.27, 2.30.0 before 2.34.12, 2.35.0 before 2.35.9, 2.36.0 before 2.36.7, and 2.37.0 before 2.37.3 contains a nil pointer dereference in the tailnet coordinator, which reads UpdateSelf.Node fields during authorization without checking that Node is set. An authenticated user or workspace agent token holder can send a CoordinateRequest with UpdateSelf present but Node empty to crash coderd, disconnecting all users on the affected replica.
items.title: Coder 2.37.0 before 2.37.3 DoS via nil Node in tailnet UpdateSelf

items.summary: pypdf before 7.0.1 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in image loading because data size estimates for some image modes are too low, defeating limits for filters without their own size limit. Attackers can craft a PDF whose images, when loaded, cause large memory usage and denial of service.
items.title: pypdf before 7.0.1 Excessive Memory Usage via Crafted PDF Images

items.summary: Frappe Framework before 15.119.0 and 16.x before 16.32.0 does not neutralize spreadsheet formula elements in user-supplied data included in CSV and XLSX exports, resulting in stored formula injection. Authenticated attackers can store crafted values that are interpreted as formulas when another user opens the exported file in a spreadsheet application.
items.title: Frappe Framework before 16.32.0 Stored Formula Injection in CSV and XLSX Exports

items.summary: SunEditor from 3.0.0 before 3.4.3 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the codeBlock plugin that allows attackers to inject script via entity-encoded pre language class values. Attackers can store content whose language- class decodes to HTML written via innerHTML into the hover button, executing script when victims hover over the block.
items.title: SunEditor 3.0.0 before 3.4.3 Stored XSS via codeBlock Language Hover Button

items.summary: web-token jwt-framework and jwt-library before 3.4.13, 4.0.x before 4.0.9, 4.1.x before 4.1.11, and 4.2.x before 4.2.6 allow CPU exhaustion because, on PHP without GMP, AbstractECDH falls back to pure PHP curve code that converts unbounded ECDH-ES epk x and y coordinates to big integers before any length check. Unauthenticated attackers who know only the recipient key's curve can send small JWEs with oversized epk coordinates, keeping workers busy for seconds to minutes per token.
items.title: web-token jwt-framework before 3.4.13 ECDH-ES DoS via Oversized epk Coordinate

items.summary: web-token jwt-framework and jwt-library before 3.4.13, 4.0.x before 4.0.9, 4.1.x before 4.1.11, and 4.2.x before 4.2.6 (and jwt-encryption through 3.2.10) do not check the key length in JWEBuilder and JWEDecrypter for direct (dir) encryption, so undersized keys are zero-padded. Anyone holding a token issued with a half-size AES-CBC-HMAC key can decrypt it, and an empty key also allows forging tokens the decrypter accepts.
items.title: web-token jwt-framework before 3.4.13 Missing Key Size Check in Direct Encryption

items.summary: web-token jwt-framework before 3.4.13, 4.0.x before 4.0.9, 4.1.x before 4.1.11, and 4.2.x before 4.2.6 allows denial of service because JWELoader and JWSLoader try every recipient or signature of a JSON General serialized token without limiting their number. Unauthenticated attackers can send a small JWE with many empty recipients inheriting a maximal PBES2 p2c value, forcing repeated key derivations that exhaust worker CPU.
items.title: Web-token jwt-framework before 3.4.13 DoS via JWE/JWS Multiple Recipients

items.summary: The LiteSpeed Cache plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.9.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires CDN Mapping to be enabled with at least one Original URLs entry containing a '*' wildcard character, a non-default configuration; the attacker's comment must also be approved, which is satisfied immediately when moderation is disabled or automatically after one prior approved comment from the same name and email address.
items.title: LiteSpeed Cache <= 7.9.3 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Comment Content via CDN URL Rewriter

items.summary: Twenty through 2.63.0 in multi-workspace mode contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain pending invitation tokens by registering an invitee's email via the signUp GraphQL mutation. Attackers can submit the leaked personalInviteToken to signUpInWorkspace to join the workspace with the invitation's role, including Admin, and obtain a verified email.
items.title: Twenty through 2.63.0 Invitation Takeover via Unauthenticated signUp Mutation

items.summary: Argo Workflows 3.0.0 through 3.7.18, 4.0.0 before 4.0.12, and 4.1.0 before 4.1.4 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the S3, GCS, and Azure Blob artifact drivers. Attackers who can write bucket objects or supply malicious artifact sources can use object keys containing ../ sequences to write arbitrary files in the executor pod, achieving code execution.
items.title: Argo Workflows 3.0.0 through 3.7.18, before 4.0.12 and 4.1.4 Path Traversal via Artifact Drivers

items.summary: Iceburg CRM through 5.0.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to view server configuration through public/v.php calling phpinfo(). Attackers can request v.php directly, bypassing Laravel routing, to obtain PHP version, extensions, INI settings, DOCUMENT_ROOT, and environment variables.
items.title: Iceburg CRM through 5.0.0 Information Disclosure via public/v.php phpinfo()

items.summary: Listmonk 4.1.0 through 7.0.0-beta.2 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in CSV subscriber import that allows list-scoped users to overwrite subscribers outside their permitted lists. Attackers holding subscribers:import and list:manage on one list can import CSV rows with victims' emails and overwrite enabled to modify names, attributes, and list memberships.
items.title: listmonk 4.1.0 through 7.0.0-beta.2 Incorrect Authorization via CSV Subscriber Import

items.summary: The CodeColorer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 0.12.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires that the attacker has already had one prior comment approved from the same name and email pair, as WordPress's comment_previously_approved check auto-approves subsequent comments from recognized commenters.
items.title: CodeColorer <= 0.12.0 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Comment Content

items.summary: The Beautiful taxonomy filters plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'term_name (reflected from DB)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.6.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires an attacker to first create a maliciously-named taxonomy term as an Author-level user; the nonce required to trigger execution is publicly emitted on any front-end page displaying the taxonomy filter widget, making the injected payload reachable by completely unauthenticated visitors.
items.title: Beautiful taxonomy filters <= 2.6.0 - Authenticated (Author+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'term_name' Parameter

items.title: shemaikuzwe Attendance_Management_system index.php sql injection

items.summary: markdownify-mcp before 1.2.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass URL validation by supplying DNS names, bracketed IPv6 literals, or IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses. Attackers can influence URLs passed to webpage-to-markdown or git-repo-to-markdown through prompt injection to fetch loopback services, internal hosts, and cloud metadata endpoints.
items.title: markdownify-mcp before 1.2.0 SSRF Protection Bypass via validateUrl and validateRepoUrl

items.summary: LightRAG provides simple and fast retrieval-augmented generation. Prior to 1.5.5, query responses are cached under a key that omits conversation_history, so an unauthenticated attacker can poison the cached answers returned to other users who send the same query. This issue is fixed in version 1.5.5.
items.title: LightRAG has unauthenticated cache poisoning of query responses due to `conversation_history` missing from query cache key

items.summary: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.15.0, Gogs does not regenerate the session ID after successful authentication. An attacker who forces a victim to use a known session ID can hijack the session after the victim logs in and take over the account. This issue is fixed in version 0.15.0.
items.title: Gogs: Session Fixation via Missing Session ID Regeneration on Sign-In

items.summary: Missing Authentication for Critical Function vulnerability in Drupal Drupal core allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels. This issue affects Drupal core versions: from 0.0.0 to 10.6.22, from 11.0.0 to 11.3.22, from 11.4.0 to 11.4.13.
items.title: Drupal core - Highly critical - Remote code execution - SA-CORE-2026-017

items.summary: Faveo Helpdesk (Community) through 2.0.3 and 2.0.4.RC.1 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in ApiExceptAuthController::checkUrl(), reachable through the unauthenticated and unthrottled GET /api/v1/helpdesk/url route, which validates the url parameter only as a well-formed URL, appends the fixed path api/v1/helpdesk/check-url and fetches it with curl with TLS certificate verification disabled and no restriction on the target host, port or address range. Unauthenticated attackers can choose the scheme, host and port of the request to make the server connect to internal hosts and services, including loopback and private addresses, and read the response body, which is returned in the JSON result field.
items.title: Faveo Helpdesk through 2.0.3 Unauthenticated SSRF via checkUrl API Endpoint

items.summary: metasfresh through 5.175 contains a SQL injection vulnerability in the stressTest_massCacheInvalidation handler of DebugRestController, which concatenates the caller-supplied tableName request parameter into SELECT statements without parameterization or validation and only checks that the caller is authenticated. Authenticated WebUI users with any role can send GET requests to /rest/api/debug/stressTest/massCacheInvalidation with SQL in the tableName parameter to run time-based and error-based blind queries against the PostgreSQL database, extracting sensitive ERP data such as user credentials and financial records while also degrading availability through sleep payloads.
items.title: metasfresh through 5.175 SQL Injection via tableName Parameter in DebugRestController

items.summary: AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. From 0.6.49 before 0.11.0, sandbox file extraction has no cumulative byte or file-count limit. A user who can run a code-execution block that extracts files can exhaust the memory of the shared workflow executor, interrupting other users' runs on it. Each file was allowed up to 50 MB based on a size that the sandbox itself reported. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.
items.title: AutoGPT: Sandbox file extraction has no cumulative byte or file-count limit

items.summary: Cron-parser through 5.10.0 contains an unbounded memory allocation vulnerability in CronExpressionParser.parse() that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust memory by supplying oversized cron fields. Attackers can submit a roughly 1.6 MB expression of repeated wildcard tokens that expand into huge arrays, exhausting the V8 heap and crashing the Node.js process.
items.title: cron-parser through 5.10.0 Unbounded Memory Allocation via CronExpressionParser.parse()

items.summary: BookStack before 26.09.3 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated Editors to permanently delete recycle bin content by converting chapters to books or books to shelves. Attackers can trigger TrashCan::destroyEntity() through the conversion actions to force-delete soft-deleted children, revisions and attachments, including content deleted by other users, preventing restoration.
items.title: BookStack before 26.09.3 Incorrect Authorization via Chapter and Book Conversion

items.summary: GNOME libxml2 2.9.10 through 2.15.4 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in xmlValidatePopElement because xmlCtxtReset frees the DTD without popping stale validation states. Attackers supplying an XML document ending inside an element to an application reusing a DTD-validating xmlTextReader can trigger heap reads, causing crashes and limited heap disclosure via error messages.
items.title: GNOME libxml2 2.9.10 through 2.15.4 Use-After-Free via xmlValidatePopElement

items.summary: Boost.JSON 1.84.0 through 1.92.0 contains an information exposure vulnerability because parser_for reset() does not reset nested parse_into handlers, retaining state across documents. Attackers controlling an abandoned or subsequent document parsed by a reused parser_for can cause partial string data from one document to appear in another's result.
items.title: Boost.JSON 1.84.0 through 1.92.0 Information Exposure via parser_for reset()

items.summary: FFmpeg through 9.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability because avcodec_flush_buffers() does not release the decoder context's frame buffer pool, so recycled buffers retain prior picture data. Attackers can supply crafted damaged streams to applications reusing one decoder context across users to recover another user's decoded picture content from unwritten frame regions.
items.title: FFmpeg through 9.1 Information Disclosure via Frame Buffer Pool Reuse

items.summary: libical 4.0.0 before 4.0.7 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in icalrecur_iterator_set_range() that allows attackers to cause denial of service by supplying crafted recurrence rules. Attackers can provide a calendar whose recurrence rule is iterated over a reverse range, causing the loop to never terminate and spin the calling thread at full CPU indefinitely.
items.title: libical 4.0.0 before 4.0.7 Infinite Loop via icalrecur_iterator_set_range

items.summary: merge-deep-composed through 0.1.4 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability in _mergeDeepOne() that allows remote attackers to modify Object.prototype by supplying __proto__ keys. Attackers can pass JSON-parsed input containing __proto__ as a merge source to inject inherited properties, causing logic bypass or denial of service in Node.js processes.
items.title: merge-deep-composed through 0.1.4 Prototype Pollution via _mergeDeepOne()

items.summary: GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 13.7.0 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with Maintainer-role permissions to obtain another user's authenticated session cookie and gain unauthorized access to that user's account due to improper session storage handling in the dependency proxy authentication flow when a redirect-pending state was triggered.
items.title: Session Fixation in GitLab

items.summary: A vulnerability was detected in slowlyo owl-admin up to 4.7.7. The impacted element is the function update of the file src/Services/AdminUserService.php of the component Admin User Management. The manipulation results in missing authorization. items.title: slowlyo owl-admin Admin User Management AdminUserService.php update authorization

items.summary: SeaweedFS is a distributed storage system for files and blobs. Prior to version 4.46, the S3 gateway does not evaluate bucket policies on POST Object uploads, which are multipart/form-data POST requests to the bucket. An authenticated S3 identity that a bucket policy restricts, such as to a key prefix or by source IP, can create or overwrite objects it is denied by sending the upload as a POST instead of a PUT. This issue has been fixed in version 4.46.
items.title: SeaweedFS S3 API: Bucket policy not enforced on POST Object uploads — an S3 identity can overwrite another identity's data

items.summary: Camunda 8.8.0 before 8.8.47, 8.9.0 before 8.9.29, 8.10.0 before 8.10.10, and 8.11.0-alpha1 contain an insecure deserialization vulnerability in the persistent web session feature, which stores session attributes as Java-serialized data in secondary storage and deserializes them via an ObjectInputStream without an ObjectInputFilter. Attackers with write access to the web session index, such as an unauthenticated Elasticsearch cluster deployed via Camunda's docker-compose files, can plant a crafted serialized object and trigger deserialization by presenting a matching session cookie, which combined with a gadget chain like the bundled Commons Collections 3.1-RC1 library can lead to code execution as the Camunda service account.
items.title: Camunda 8 Insecure Deserialization via Web Session Storage

items.summary: Nmap before 7.992 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in the process_write function of the NSE tn3270.lua library, whose write loop does not advance when it processes a malformed Repeat to Address (RA) order. A malicious TN3270 server on a scanned host can embed a single 6-byte malformed RA order in an ordinary screen-write data stream after a normal negotiation, causing a permanent 100% CPU hang of the Nmap process when tn3270-screen.nse runs, which the script-timeout option does not interrupt.
items.title: Nmap < 7.992 Infinite Loop via Malformed Repeat to Address Order in tn3270.lua

items.summary: Nmap before 7.992 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in the ConfCreateResponse GCC block parser of the NSE rdp.lua library, which does not check that each block advances the read position. A malicious RDP server on a scanned host can include a single malformed zero-length block in an otherwise valid handshake, causing a permanent 100% CPU hang of the Nmap process that the script-timeout option does not interrupt; the library is used by rdp-enum-encryption.nse in the default script category (-sC, -A).
items.title: Nmap < 7.992 Infinite Loop via Zero-Length GCC Block in rdp.lua

items.summary: Nmap before 7.992 contains a hardcoded cryptographic key vulnerability in the DHCAST128 login of the NSE afp.lua library, which uses a fixed, publicly known Diffie-Hellman private exponent. A passive observer of the network traffic between Nmap and an Apple Filing Protocol server can compute the shared secret from the hardcoded exponent and the server's public value and decrypt the password supplied to scripts such as afp-showmount.nse and afp-brute.nse through the afp.username and afp.password arguments, without man-in-the-middle access or cryptanalysis.
items.title: Nmap < 7.992 Cleartext Credential Recovery via Hardcoded DH Exponent in afp.lua

items.title: LibrePhotos ExifTool Metadata Write-Back writer.py write_metadata argument injection

items.summary: Ever Gauzy is an open source business management platform for ERP, CRM, HRM, ATS, and project management. Prior to 111.42.13, POST /api/integration/github/webhook in packages/plugins/integration-github/src/lib/probot/probot.discovery.ts passes request bodies through ProbotDiscovery.receiveHook to probot.receive without verifying x-hub-signature-256 against the configured webhook secret. Because the route is public and uses the attacker-controlled installation.id to locate integrations, an unauthenticated remote attacker who knows or guesses an installation identifier can forge installation deletion events that remove a tenant's GitHub integration or forge issues events that insert fabricated issue data into the tenant's automation pipeline. This issue is fixed in version 111.42.13.
items.title: Ever Gauzy: GitHub App webhook receiver never verifies HMAC signature — forgeable events allow unauthenticated tenant-integration deletion and fake issue injection

items.summary: VeraCrypt through 1.26.31 on Linux contains an improper path restriction vulnerability in the elevated CoreService, which passes the path and owner UID from a SetFileOwnerRequest directly to chown() in CoreUnix::SetFileOwner without target validation on Linux. An attacker with an active elevated CoreService session and same-UID access who reopens the request pipe through /proc/<pid>/fd/<n> can take ownership of arbitrary system files such as /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow, achieving full root compromise.
items.title: VeraCrypt through 1.26.31 Improper Path Restriction via CoreService chown()

items.summary: VeraCrypt before 1.26.30 on Linux contains a command injection vulnerability in CoreUnix::CheckFilesystem that allows a local attacker with same-UID access and an active elevated CoreService session to execute arbitrary commands by injecting an unsanitized VirtualDevice value into a shell command string. Attackers can reopen the request pipe through /proc/<pid>/fd/<n> and supply a crafted VirtualDevice value such as /dev/null; <command> to achieve arbitrary command execution as root.
items.title: VeraCrypt before 1.26.30 Command Injection via CoreUnix::CheckFilesystem

items.title: GongShengyue OnlineBooks BooksServlet BooksServlet.java listSplit missing authentication
